data.summary: This batch reports 2 responses side by side and 1 batch overlay across them; 2 of 3 inferential findings show evidence at their alpha.
sentences: This batch reports 2 responses side by side and 1 batch overlay across them; 2 of 3 inferential findings show evidence at their alpha.
Request 1 reports 1 test from 96 of 100 records.
Request 1's test 1 (TEST_T) labelled `score by plan` finds no evidence of a difference at alpha 0.05 (p = 0.3). Its effect size `cohens_d` is 0.1, very small by the convention of Cohen (1988).
Request 1's run read 100 records; 96 passed the filters and 0 were left out for a missing value.
Request 2 reports 1 test and aggregated output of 9 rows across 1 group from 9 of 10 records.
Request 2's test 1 (TEST_T) labelled `score by plan` finds evidence of a difference at alpha 0.05 (p = 0.01). Its effect size `cohens_d` is 0.6, medium by the convention of Cohen (1988).
Request 2's aggregation 1 `total` is reported without its request, so its operator is not named. Its value is 12. It read 9 rows and left out 0 with no value.
Request 2's run read 10 records; 9 passed the filters and 0 were left out for a missing value.
The batch's overlay 1 (OVERLAY_T_CELL) `plan cells` runs 3 tests; 1 of them falls below alpha 0.05 after the holm adjustment over its compose family.
caveats: 2 p-values here carry no adjustment for multiple comparisons, so some may fall below alpha by chance alone; this is the concern the PULSE_ADVISORY_MANY_TESTS advisory raises.
Adding a multiplicity block (for example holm) adjusts them for multiple comparisons; then read p_adjusted beside each raw p-value.
Partial reading: the composed request is absent, so the aggregations and groupings are described by count only; pass it beside the response to name their operators and weight.
TEST_T: Rows are independent of each other, within and across groups.
TEST_T: The two-group version uses Welch's correction, so the groups need not have equal variances.
TEST_T: The average is roughly normally distributed: safe for large groups, risky for small skewed ones.
TEST_T: The p-value is two-sided: it looks for a difference in either direction.

OVERLAY_T_CELL: Cells must use AGG_WELFORD, which supplies each cell's mean, variance and n. Without it the test uses one variance and n per side for every cell (params variance_target / variance_ref / sample_size_target / sample_size_ref, default variance 1 and n 2). Those p-values describe the values you supplied, not each cell's own spread, and they change with the measure's units.
OVERLAY_T_CELL: Target and reference are separate, independent samples. Equal variances are not assumed, and each mean should be roughly normal.
OVERLAY_T_CELL: The null hypothesis is equal means in the cell; the p-value is two-sided.

OVERLAY_T_CELL: Every cell is a separate test, so with many cells some small p-values turn up by luck; to adjust for multiple comparisons, set multiplicity on the overlay (holm or bonferroni hold the family-wise error, bh or by the false discovery rate) to add adjusted p-values beside the raw ones.
